name: Recording voltmeter
summary: Recording instrument that keeps a time record of voltage, drawn as a square marked V.
description: A recording voltmeter stores voltage against time so that sags, swells and slow variations can be reviewed later. On single-line diagrams it is drawn off a VT secondary at a busbar or supply point, and on schematics it is wired across the VT circuit like an indicating voltmeter.

The symbol does not say how fast the recorder samples. A slow recorder logging averages every few minutes cannot show short dips, so the recording interval must be checked against what the record will be used to investigate.
readingNotes: Identify the VT feeding the recorder.
Check the recording interval against the events of interest.
distinction: A recording voltmeter stores a time record; an ordinary voltmeter shows only the present voltage.
